definitions.explanation: The sea between the Japanese archipelago and the Asian mainland. In Japanese usage it also evokes a whole climate and mood: grey winter skies, rough water, and heavy snow on the coast facing it.

examples.japanese: {日本海|にほんかい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{荒|あ}れる→荒れる：04577_areru⟧。
examples.english: The Sea of Japan gets rough in winter.
The Sea of Japan side of the country gets a lot of snow.

examples.japanese: {日本海|にほんかい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{取|と}れた→取れる：02376_toreru⟧カニ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{味覚|みかく}→味覚：04424_mikaku⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{送|おく}られる→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: Crab caught in the Sea of Japan is shipped nationwide as a taste of winter.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {日本海|にほんかい}⟦{側|がわ}→〜側：03090_gawa⟧: the Sea of Japan side (of Honshu)
- {日本海|にほんかい}⟦{沿岸|えんがん}→沿岸：13280_engan⟧: the Sea of Japan coast
- {日本海|にほんかい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{荒|あ}れる→荒れる：04577_areru⟧: the Sea of Japan turns rough

CULTURAL NOTE:
{日本海|にほんかい}⟦{側|がわ}→〜側：03090_gawa⟧ and ⟦{太平洋|たいへいよう}→太平洋：09680_taiheiyou⟧⟦{側|がわ}→〜側：03090_gawa⟧ are the standard way of dividing Japan's weather. Winter winds pick up moisture over the Sea of Japan and drop it as some of the world's heaviest snowfall on the western coast, while the Pacific side stays dry and sunny — so the two phrases carry a whole picture of climate, food, and daily life.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{太平洋|たいへいよう}→太平洋：09680_taiheiyou⟧: the Pacific Ocean — the paired term in almost every weather report
- ⟦{瀬戸内海|せとないかい}→瀬戸内海：30793_setonaikai⟧: the Seto Inland Sea — calm and sheltered, the opposite image
